diagnosis_ab10_meander_ab11_turn_and_ste.answer: Neither a heel/toe swap, nor a relabel, nor a heading flip, nor a real segment branch. The published foot angle is physically fine for 98 to 99.7 percent of the samples; the 'foot 180 degrees from the shank for thousands of samples' is created by the unwrap itself. A sagittal angle of a nearly flat foot is ill-defined for a few samples when the foot's heading is about 90 degrees from the pelvis heading; the published value then passes through +-180 for those samples only, and np.unwrap carries a whole-turn offset (-360, and -720 later in AB11) through the rest of the recording.

evidence_ab10_meander_1_right_foot.markers: RCAL, RMT1, RMT5 (toe = mean of MT1, MT5), pelvis heading from LASI/RASI
evidence_ab10_meander_1_right_foot.foot_length_m: 0.201 at index 1930, 0.201 at 1955, 0.200 at 1960, 0.200 at 1975; whole recording median 0.203, min 0.183, max 0.207 (no jump)
evidence_ab10_meander_1_right_foot.largest_one_sample_change_of_the_heel_to: 2.1 degrees in the whole recording (a heel/toe swap or relabel would be about 180)
evidence_ab10_meander_1_right_foot.reading: at 90 degrees of foot yaw the projection of the 0.2 m foot onto the pelvis forward axis goes through zero and the vertical component is about 1 mm, so the in-plane vector is tiny and its angle sweeps 140 degrees in 5 samples (25 ms). Afterwards the foot yaw is back inside 90 degrees and the published angle is normal again (+8.7, -6.9). The pelvis heading itself is smooth (pelvis velocity versus heading 137 to 131 degrees, no sudden flip) so no ASIS relabel.
evidence_ab10_meander_1_right_foot.fraction_of_samples: foot yaw beyond 90 degrees from the pelvis heading in 2 percent of the stretch (median 29 degrees, max 96); published |sagittal angle| above 90 degrees in 2 percent of the stretch and 1.8 percent of the recording; the two criteria agree on 100 percent of stretch samples; outside the stretch 0.3 percent

evidence_ab11_turn_and_step_1_left_foot.foot_length_m: 0.188 to 0.193 at the start of the stretch, median 0.194, range 0.167 to 0.209; one-sample direction change at most 3.3 degrees
evidence_ab11_turn_and_step_1_left_foot.reading: same mechanism; the second excursion at 21679 is another crossing of 90 degrees of foot yaw, which is why E02 carries two whole turns after that point

diagnosis_ab10_meander_ab11_turn_and_ste.e02_unwrapped_values_vs_published: AB10 right foot: published -6.9 at 3000 became -366.9 (-1 turn), -31.8 became -391.8 at 5000; 7,200 of 9,160 samples carry -1 turn; E02 foot angle ends at -483 and 78.6 percent of the samples lie outside +-180. AB11 left foot: -11.2 became -371.2 at 15000, -19.5 became -739.5 at 22000; offsets -1 turn for 6,737 samples and -2 turns for 2,454 samples (38.1 percent outside +-180); range to -805. In both the foot is flat and normal at those samples.
diagnosis_ab10_meander_ab11_turn_and_ste.consequence: The unwrap is wrong for these two recordings: it takes sudden ill-conditioned sweeps for a continuous rotation and shifts the rest of the recording. It also produces the 20 new AB11 phase L1 failures (the left ankle reads to -773 degrees).
diagnosis_ab10_meander_ab11_turn_and_ste.recommendation_for_jose: Return these two recordings (AB10 meander_1 right foot and right ankle, AB11 turn_and_step_1 left foot and left ankle) to the published (+-180) values from C06, i.e. no unwrap there. Optional second step, also his call: hold only the roughly 2 percent (AB10) and 0.3 percent (AB11) of samples where the foot heading is more than 90 degrees from the pelvis heading and the sagittal angle is ill-defined. The AB13 dynamic_walk_1 wrap (one sample, shank near -135 degrees, foot near -180) is a different, genuine branch cut and its unwrap is right (see below).
diagnosis_ab10_meander_ab11_turn_and_ste.other_unwrap_check_ab13: AB13 dynamic_walk_1 right foot: published 179.95 then -179.98 degrees (wrapped step 0.07 degrees) across samples 19258/19259 with a heel-kick shank at -135 degrees; one isolated crossing, not a singularity. The one-sample change is a true wrap and E02 fixes it.
